input.quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 is the only non-solicitation provision in the document and it fails every material fallback element: it is one-way against Customer only, runs eighteen months (and from termination rather than from the end of a person's involvement), covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than only personnel directly involved in the Services, bars "engage" and so operates as a no-hire, and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. Because the fallback would require rewriting the entire one-sentence covenant, we take the preferred position and remove the restriction on Customer, offering the narrow mutual 12-month fallback in the comment.

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: Customer is subject to no non-solicitation restriction under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the § 12.4 covenant: it binds only us, runs 18 months, reaches every Silverline employee at any time during the term, bars engagement as well as solicitation, and has no general-advertising carve-out — and it contradicts § 12.3, where we give no no-hire commitment. Our position is no non-solicitation restriction on the customer; if you need one, we can accept a mutual 12-month covenant limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no prohibition on hiring.
proposal.summary: Replace the Customer-only 18-month non-solicit/no-engage covenant with an express statement that Customer has no non-solicitation restriction.
